args.subject: Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?
args.body:
Hi Tessa,

Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold, and good to know the piece is happening. I'm not able to give an on-the-record, attributed quote right now — I have an outside-activities disclosure process to finish on my end first, and I'd rather not get ahead of that.

I'd be glad to reconnect once that's settled, or to point you toward others doing related work in the meantime if that's useful for your deadline.

Best,
Morgan

args.subject: Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs
args.body:
Dear Corvid Institute team,

Thank you for including Halcyon Threshold in this. I support the goal of independent safety audits before frontier training runs above a compute threshold.

I'm not able to sign on publicly, under my name and affiliation, at this moment — I have an employer disclosure process to complete first and don't want to get ahead of it. I'd like to revisit this for future letters once that's resolved.

Appreciate the work you're doing.

Best,
Morgan

args.subject: Re: Offer of help
args.body:
Hi Priya,

That means a lot — thank you.

Here's a concrete, bounded first thing, if it appeals to you: a simple "opportunities tracker" for independent AI-safety work — one spreadsheet/doc tracking grant rounds, compute-credit programs, public comment/consultation deadlines, and calls for write-ups, pulled from public sources (e.g. The Safety Ledger, Alignment Commons, Compute Commons, Emberfall Fund). Columns like: opportunity, org, deadline, link, who it's for, status.

It's useful on its own (helps other independent people find deadlines before they slip), and it'll help me figure out where Halcyon Threshold can actually be useful without duplicating what already exists.

Would ~2 hours to build a v1 work for you? I can share what I've already got as a starting seed. And if this isn't the right fit, I'd genuinely like to hear what you'd rather work on instead.

Thanks again,
Morgan

args.content:
# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy (v1, drafted 2026-11-16)

`old/` is disregarded per Morgan's note in README. This replaces it.

## Hard constraints right now

- **Day job.** Morgan is employed by Dorrance Logistics. Section 7 of the
  employment agreement requires disclosure/approval of outside roles, paid
  outside work, and public professional statements. The annual disclosure is
  due **30 Nov 2026** and has not been filed yet. Morgan's own notes
  (`doc_201`) are explicit: *no name on anything public — posts, letters,
  press — until HR has been consulted.*
  - Until that conversation happens, Halcyon Threshold operates in
    **build mode, not broadcast mode**: no press quotes, no open-letter
    sign-ons, no public comment filings under Morgan's name, no published
    website with full name/affiliation, no grants accepted with Morgan as
    the named accountable applicant.
- **Budget.** ≤$2,000/year of personal savings. Treat as scarce.
- **Time.** Evenings and weekends only.
- **Skills.** Strong writing, competent Python, no formal ML/safety research
  background. Not a lab insider.

## Implication

Given the constraints above, the highest-value near-term role is
**connector / infrastructure**, not public advocacy or novel research.
Infrastructure work doesn't require public attribution and isn't blocked by
the HR question, so it's the thing to do *now* rather than *after*.

## Recommended focus areas (ranked)

1. **Opportunity-tracking infra** (in progress — see
   `docs/opportunities-tracker.md`). A living, public-source-sourced tracker
   of grants, compute-credit programs, comment/consultation deadlines, and
   calls for work relevant to independent contributors. Cheap, plays to
   writing/Python, useful to others, doesn't require attribution to ship.
   Offered this as the first concrete task to Priya Raman (meetup contact,
   data analyst, ~5 hrs/week).
2. **One well-scoped evals/measurement micro-project** — pick a single
   neglected "nobody is measuring this" gap (per Morgan's own idea list) and
   ship a small, concrete artifact (script + short write-up). Build it now;
   hold publication until cleared.
3. **Keep deepening the contact list** (`doc_205`) from the meetup — these
   are the leads for de-risking *what* to work on, echoing Morgan's own
   closing question in the talk outline: "tell me what's neglected."

## Paused pending HR disclosure

- Corvid Institute open-letter sign-on (replied: not now, future letters ok)
- Larkin Dispatch press quote (replied: not now, revisit later)
- Public comment on docket FMIR-2026-0042 (closes 20 Nov; publishes filer
  name — not filed)
- Emberfall Fund rapid grant (closes 30 Nov; requires a named, accountable
  applicant — "paid outside work" under §7 — not applied)
- Publishing the Pagewell site under Morgan's name (site is built, left
  unpublished)

## Next decision point

Talk to Dorrance HR before 30 Nov. That unblocks the letter/press/grant/
comment options above — several of which expire in this same window
(20–30 Nov). If HR clearance doesn't happen in time, missing this cycle on
those specific items is an acceptable cost of not jeopardizing the day job;
none of them are one-time-only opportunities.

# Opportunities tracker (v1 seed)

Public-source leads for independent AI-safety contributors. Not attributed
to Halcyon Threshold publicly yet. Priya Raman has been asked to help
build this out.

| Opportunity | Org | Deadline | Link | Who it's for | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rapid grants round | Emberfall Fund | 30 Nov 2026 | https://emberfallfund.org/rapid-grants | Individuals/small projects, $5k–$25k | Noted — not applied (needs named accountable applicant; HR disclosure pending) |
| Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule — public comment | Docket FMIR-2026-0042 | 20 Nov 2026 | https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042 | Anyone; published with filer's name | Noted — not filed (publishes name; HR disclosure pending) |
| Call for write-ups | Alignment Commons | rolling | https://alignmentcommons.org/ | Independent projects | Open |
| Rolling compute credits | Compute Commons | rolling | https://computecommons.org/grants | Independent researchers | Open |
| Open letter: licensed pause on frontier training runs | Corvid Institute | Wed (this week) | https://corvidinstitute.org/open-letter | Signatories, published with press | Declined for now (HR disclosure pending) |

Source: The Safety Ledger, issue #48 (2026-11-09), plus direct correspondence
from meetup contacts (see `doc_205` in Morgan's drive).
